примитивные-типы-данных.p1: In JS, every variable has a value. A **primitive** data type is the data type of a variable with its name directly attached to its value.
примитивные-типы-данных.p2: However, the value of a variable can be a **reference**. We call such data types **reference** data types. We'll look at the reference data type next.
string.p1: A string is an ordered set of characters that are enclosed in double (⟦f2⟧) or single (⟦f3⟧) quotes.
string.p4: You can also wrap a string in backquotes **⟦f4⟧**, but backquotes are usually used for [►►►**template literals**►►►](⟦f5⟧).
string.p5: If double quotes occur within a string, the string itself must be wrapped in single quotes, and vice versa.

string.p10: The widest range of characters from various alphabets is represented in the UTF-8 encoding (Unicode Transformation Format, 8-bit).

nan.p1: ![ico-20 warn] The value **⟦f29⟧** can occur when trying to perform arithmetic operations with operands that aren't numbers and can't be converted to a number, like ⟦f30⟧, as well as when attempting to divide zero by zero: ⟦f31⟧.
nan.p2: ![ico-20 warn] The value **⟦f32⟧** is not equal to any other value, including itself.
nan.p3: ![ico-20 warn] No arithmetic operations in JS will ever result in an error, because if there's an error, the operation will return **⟦f33⟧**.
